**STEP 1 - Scene:** A small side of sliced cucumber on a white paper plate, photographed from almost directly overhead. The plate sits on a sheet with QR codes, so this looks like a takeaway or cafeteria-style side dish.

**STEP 2 - Ruler:** The plate is a roughly square paper plate about 20 cm across. Taking it as a 20 cm diameter gives an area of about 314 cm².

**STEP 3 - Items:** Cucumber, cut into half-moon and wedge pieces (about 18 pieces). A few tiny yellowish specks, probably seasoning or dressing residue, are too small to weigh.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The cucumber pieces cover about 15% of the plate, roughly 47 cm². The pile is loose, so the gaps are large.

**STEP 5 - Volume:** The pile is about 1.5 cm high at its outer envelope. 47 cm² × 1.5 cm ≈ 70 ml.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Cut vegetables have a bulk density of about 0.6 g/ml. 70 ml × 0.6 ≈ 42 g. Counting pieces at about 3 g each (18 × 3 ≈ 54 g) gives a similar figure, so I take about 50 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Raw cucumber is about 15 kcal/100 g. 50 g × 0.15 ≈ 8 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** A small handful of cucumber slices weighing about 50 g and providing under 10 kcal is plausible. There is no visible oil, dressing, or other energy-dense food.
